document.title: Your Meeting with Pakistani President Musharraf
document.authors: U.S. Department of State (Secretary Powell to President Bush)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret] Powell highlights changes in U.S.-Pakistan relations since 9/11: cooperation on counterterrorism, nuclear nonproliferation and economic development. Musharraf has abandoned the Taliban at political risk and is concerned the Northern Alliance will occupy Kabul. Previously released in 2010.

mentions.quote: President Musharraf's decision to fully cooperate with the United States in the wake of September 11, at considerable political risk
Musharraf is pressing for a future government supportive of its interests and is concerned that the Northern Alliance will occupy Kabul.
Musharraf's making good on his pledge to hold free and fair
During my October 15-16 visit to Islamabad, I affirmed our renewed relationship
Your meeting and dinner can serve to assure Musharraf we will assist Pakistan through this difficult time

events.description: Powell visited Islamabad Oct 15-16 and discussed defeating terrorists and rebuilding Afghanistan with Musharraf.
Terrorist attack on the Kashmir state assembly killed 38 civilians.
Powell memo to President Bush on meeting with Musharraf.
Terrorist attack on the state assembly in Kashmir killed 38 civilians; India subsequently shelled.
Powell visited Islamabad (Oct 15-16) and met Musharraf, discussing counterterrorism, Afghanistan, proliferation.
Under Secretary Al Larson traveled to Islamabad to discuss assistance, trade and debt.
Powell memo to Bush on meeting with Musharraf.
US provides $100m budgetary support, $500m planned, $73m border security aid; sanctions relief signed into law.
Musharraf decided to fully cooperate with the US after September 11, abandoning the Taliban.

key_claims: Musharraf's post-9/11 cooperation turned the stalled US-Pakistan relationship around.
Musharraf abandoned the Taliban and froze terrorist assets.
Pakistan wants a post-Taliban government supportive of its interests and fears Northern Alliance control of Kabul.
Kashmir tensions threaten US efforts in Afghanistan.
The US is providing substantial economic and military assistance to Pakistan.
